posts.author: Andrew76
posts.content_md:
Hello,

New to the board and a hologram noob as well. After visiting the Museum of Holography in Chicago I was blown away with the 3d realism of the holographic artwork. I highly recomend visiting it if your in the area. I have been doing a lot of reading and searching but I haven't found a lot of info on backlit holograms. Also, It seems like most holograms are really small and I was interested in making large holograms up to 24" x 36"

And finally I wanted to bring a character created in MAYA (a 3d modeling program) to life as a large backlit hologram. I know that these are advanced ideas and I need to walk before I can run but maybe you can point me in the right direction to achieving this goal. Is there a beginner kit for making backlit holograms? Thanks for your help!

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: A backlit hologram is simply a transmission hologram. You may want to start there. Check out the HoloWiki for more information. The link is at the top of the page.

24x26" is a lot of energy. You will need to have a large laser. A 100mw C315 would do it if you made a very nice table but better would be a large Ar+ laser.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
I hate to add it up but I am sure I have spent upwards of $10K. I have not spent my money wisely but I do have some cool toys. 

A high power AR+ laser would run about $5 to 10K with an etelon. Augie Muth often has a laser or two for sale. 

[http://www.lasart.com](http://www.lasart.com)
